answer: In a PoA economy each agent’s identity is anchored to a reputation canyon formed by cryptographic proofs of work and cross‑signed attestations; any new node must climb this canyon by contributing verifiable tasks. A jetty of honeypot challenges, released during a network gale, forces the candidate to answer randomly generated verification queries that only genuine agents can solve without collusion. An attacker must generate millions of costly proofs and solve each honeypot, inflating resource expenditure beyond feasible sybil scaling.
